title: Safa and Marwa
hook: walking seven times between the hills, as Hajar ran

segments.voice: Yesterday, Zamzam, and your line: drink with intention. What did you name before your glass of water? Day one thousand one hundred twenty-nine.

A woman stands on top of a small rocky hill, shading her eyes, looking out over an empty valley. Her water is gone. Her baby is crying below. She sees nobody. So she comes down, crosses the low ground, running where the valley dips, and climbs the hill on the other side. She looks again. Nobody. Back she goes. The woman is Hajar, and the story is told by Ibn Abbas in Sahih al-Bukhari. Today, the walk that pilgrims make in her footsteps.
screen: `A WOMAN ON A HILL.` → `HER WATER IS GONE.` → `SHE RUNS TO THE OTHER HILL.`

segments.voice: First, her story. In Ibn Abbas's telling, Ibrahim leaves Hajar and their baby, Ismail, in the valley with a little food and water. She follows him and asks: has Allah commanded you to do this? He says yes. And she answers, then He will not abandon us. When the water runs out, she climbs Safa, then Marwa, back and forth, looking for help, seven times. At the end, she hears a sound, and the water of yesterday's well breaks out of the ground. Second, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ's comment, kept in the same report: that is why people walk between the two. Her searching became their rite. Third, what the Qur'an says. In Pickthall's translation of surah two: "Lo! (the mountains) As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the indications of Allah." Jabir, in Sahih Muslim, says that when the Prophet came near Safa, he recited that verse and said, I begin with what Allah began with. So the walk starts at Safa, as the verse does. Fourth, the walk today. The two hills are now inside the mosque, joined by a long covered corridor. Pilgrims walk from one end to the other, seven lengths in all, and in the low stretch between, marked out for them, the men hurry, the way she ran where the valley dipped. Look at who sets the pace here. Not a prophet, not a king. A mother, alone, worried, doing everything she could do while she trusted that she wouldn't be abandoned. The pilgrims, whoever they are at home, walk behind her.
screen: `THEN HE WILL NOT ABANDON US.` · `HER SEARCH BECAME THEIR RITE.` · `SAFA AND MARWA, SIGNS OF ALLAH.` · `THE PILGRIMS WALK BEHIND HER.`

segments.voice: The practice: walk seven lengths of a room. Choose two points, a door and a window, a wall and a chair. Start at one, and walk to the other. That's one. Walk back. That's two. Go on until you've made seven, counting as you go. On one stretch in the middle, quicken your step a little, the way she ran. If you pray, you can make du'a as you walk, in your own words. If you don't, hold someone in mind who is searching for something right now. Then stop, and breathe. The bell holds the time.
Sa'y. The walk between Safa and Marwa, seven lengths, in Hajar's footsteps. Today's word.
Your line: in her footsteps. Today, do one thing you can do about a worry, then trust the rest. Day one thousand one hundred twenty-nine.

howItsDone: After tawaf, pilgrims perform sa'y: seven lengths between Safa and Marwa, starting at Safa and ending at Marwa, now inside a long gallery of the sacred mosque, with men hurrying between the green markers.
